newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

A meeting of the nine Test cricket captains in London today will discuss the prospect of badly behaved cricket players accumulating demerit points that would ultimately lead to their suspension. The meeting is the result of a proposal to further the Interational Cricket Council's code of conduct. Page 16.

Australia's number one women's tennis player Annabel Ellwood says this weekend's Federation Cup clash against Spain is vital to her career after losing in the first round of her past eight tournaments this year. Australian coach Liz Smylie says Ellwood's form has hit a flat spot but says it is all part of the learning process for the 19-year-old. Page 16.

Australian Cyclists Stuart O'Grady and Robbie McEwen have finished in the top ten riders in the Tour de France ride from Plumelec to Le Puy du Fou. The placings make it the third time in four days Australian riders have made the top ten. Page 17.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian test cricketer Shane Warne arrived back in Australia yesterday, for a leave of absence from the Ashes tour to see new daughter Brooke and wife Simone, defending his off-field actions after Australia's third Test win. He has been criticised for is one-fingered gesture from the Australian's balcony to the English spectators. Page 46.

England Rugby Union coach Jack Rowell has been the subject of intensifying pressure as rumours surface that British lions leader Ian McGeechan, Auckland's Graham Henry or Australia's Bob Dwyer may take over the British coaching role. To make the situation worse, Rowell is set to lose star player Tony Underwood from the side to play Australia in a one-off test match on Saturday night. Page 46.

Defending champions Australia have notched up a semi-final berth in the women's world under-20 basketball championship in Natal, Brazil, after beating Cuba 91-58. Australia has won three out of four games to be in second place behind the US at the end of he penultimate day of pool competition. Page 45.
THE AGE

The woes of Geelong star Gary Ablett are set to continue after ProSquad chief Craig Kelly said yesterday his marketing group would not pick up Ablett's affairs. ProSquad is in direct competition with Flying Start, Ablett's current marketing company, but says when Ablett is dropped from their list they will not pick him up. Page D3.

Australian tennis players Mark Woodforde and Sandon Stolle are both through to the third round at the Hall of Fame tennis championships at Newport Rhode Island, after scoring straight set wins. Woodforde and Stolle are seeded number two and number four repectively. Page D13.

The Country Racing Council in Victoria has announced all clubs will reduce prize money by up to ten per cent in the coming season. The change comes as a forerunner to even greater changes that will take place after all clubs are scrutinised at the end of ext season. Page D11.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian Football League club Essendon is set to name Darren Bewick in the team line-up to play Sydney on Sunday. Bewick has not played since March when he ruptured the medial ligament in his left knee in a match against Adelaide in Alice Springs. Page 02.

Australian Football league umpires have lodged claims in the Industrial Relations Commission asking for security of employment, higher wages and better working conditions. The meeting of umpires demands mean the AFL would have to add more than $A360,000 t its budget for next season. Page 100.

Australian motor racing legend Peter Brock says he is determined to enter into Sunday's round of the Australian Touring Car Championships with a relaxed attitude after he unexpectedly won the last round as a result of this approach. Brock also suggested sme of his younger collegues should relax into driving instead of getting up tight. Page 93.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Boxer Mike Tyson has been handed down the largest fine and toughest penalty ever given to a boxer after he bit Evander Holyfield's ear in a title fight last week. Tyson has been fined $US4 million and ordered to pay the administrative costs of the tribuna hearing, hoever, many believe he has got off lightly with expectations he will be back fighting in a year. Page 120.

Embattled Australian athletics star Dean Capobianco has revealed he was broke and had to go without food on some days during his fight to get a drug suspension overruled. The two-time Olympic sprinter said during an interview to be aired on Optus Vision on Monday that his life has changed dramatically since the time he owned 3 Porsches. Page 118.

Australian netball vice-captain Carissa Tombs is likely to be out of the game for six weeks after she undergoes surgery on a freak knee injury she sustained on Wednesday night. Tombs twisted her knee in the air in a match between Manly Warringah and the Astralian Institute of Sport. Page 115.
